1. Single points of contact

1.1 For authorities (Article 11)

Member States' authorities, the European Commission and the European Board for Digital Services reach DressYou's single point of contact by email at [[FOUNDER: authority-contact — the electronic address of the point of contact for authorities]]. They may write in French or in English. [[COUNSEL: contact-points — May one monitored mailbox serve Article 11, Article 12 and the terrorist-content contact point, and are French and English the right languages to state? Counsel brief B1, B8.]]

1.2 For users and anyone else (Article 12)

Anyone who uses DressYou, with or without an account, reaches DressYou in the app through support, or by email at [[FOUNDER: user-contact — the electronic address of the point of contact for users and people without an account]]. Messages may be written in French or in English. Neither route relies on automated tools alone: you can always reach a person at DressYou. [[FOUNDER: contact-staffing — Who reads these messages, and what response time does DressYou state? §4.15 asks for an honest stated expectation.]]

1.3 For removal orders on terrorist content

Competent authorities send removal orders under Regulation (EU) 2021/784 to [[FOUNDER: removal-order-contact — the electronic address that receives removal orders, and who acts on it within the hour, including outside office hours]], in French or in English. DressYou removes the terrorist content, or disables access to it in all Member States, within one hour of receiving the order.

2. Reporting content: the notice form (Article 16)

2.1 Who can report, and where

Anyone can report content in DressYou, with or without an account: a post, a comment, a profile or an ask page. The form opens from the report link on each of them and from the website [[FOUNDER: notice-form-location — the address of the form on dressyouapp.com]]. A person reviews every report made from an account and every notice.

2.2 The form

Report content to DressYou

You can report content you consider illegal, or content that breaks the DressYou terms of use. A person at DressYou reviews every report.

  1. What are you reporting? Paste the link to the post, comment, profile or ask page, or start from its own report link, which fills this in. If the post has several photographs, say which one.

  2. Why are you reporting it? Choose the reason that fits best:

    • I appear in this photograph and did not agree to it
    • Child sexual abuse material
    • A threat to someone's life or safety
    • Sexual content
    • Text that disparages someone's body
    • Harassment
    • Impersonation, or a fake account
    • Not the poster's own photograph, or a generated image
    • It infringes my rights, such as my copyright or my image
    • Spam, or engagement manufactured to earn rewards
    • Other illegal content
    • Another breach of the terms of use

    [[FOUNDER: notice-reasons — Confirm this reason list. Today's report queue holds body_disparaging, not_the_poster, generated_image, sexual_content, harassment, spam_or_commercial and other.]]

  3. Explain why. Say what the item shows or says, and why it is illegal or breaks the terms of use. If you consider it illegal, name the law if you know it.
  4. Your name and email address. DressYou uses them to confirm receipt and to send you its decision. You may leave them out when you report child sexual abuse material.
  5. Your statement. A box to tick: “I believe in good faith that the information and allegations in this report are accurate and complete.”

[[COUNSEL: notice-knowledge — Does a notice made with this form give DressYou actual knowledge under Article 16(3), is a web form with email enough, and how fast must DressYou act on body imagery? Counsel brief B3, A4(2).]]

2.3 After a notice

If you gave an email address, DressYou confirms receipt without undue delay, then sends you its decision, says whether automated means were used, and explains how to contest it (section 3.12). DressYou does not give your name to the person whose content you reported unless that is strictly necessary.

DressYou's review targets: an item reported in a serious category is hidden at once and reviewed within 24 hours; other reports are reviewed within 72 hours. [[FOUNDER: serious-categories — Which reasons count as serious, with the item hidden as soon as it is reported?]]

A report of known child sexual abuse material follows the reporting route the law sets. [[COUNSEL: csam-reporting — Which vendor may match known child sexual abuse material, how and where must a match or a notice be reported, and must the statement of reasons to the poster wait for the authority? §10, decision of 13 October 2026.]]

3. Statements of reasons (Article 17)

3.1 When DressYou sends one

DressYou sends a statement of reasons to the person concerned whenever it removes their content, hides it during review, keeps a held post unpublished, suspends or closes their account, or withholds their rewards, on the ground that the content is illegal or breaks the terms of use. Each statement is recorded with the decision. [[FOUNDER: statement-channel — Does the statement arrive in the app, by email, or both?]] [[COUNSEL: interim-measures — Do a hold before publication and a hide during review each need a statement of reasons, or only the final decision?]]

Showing a post lower to one viewer because no size of its garment fits that viewer is not a measure against the post, in DressYou's reading, and no statement is sent. [[COUNSEL: fit-ranking — Does Article 17 reach this ordering? Counsel brief B4(1).]]

3.2 What every statement contains

Every statement has the same parts, filled from the decision record:

  1. The decision: the measure, worded as in sections 3.4 to 3.10, with its territorial scope and its duration.
  2. The item: a link to the content or the account concerned, and the date of the decision.
  3. The facts: what started the review, whether a report from an account, a notice, automatic screening or DressYou's own review, and what the reviewer found.
  4. The ground: for illegal content, the law relied on and why the content breaks it; for a breach of the terms of use, the section relied on and why the content breaks it (section 3.13).
  5. Automated means: whether automatic screening detected the item. A hold before review is automatic; every final decision is taken by a person.
  6. Redress: the appeal (section 3.3) and the courts.

The templates below name a post; for a comment or a profile, the same text names the comment or the profile.

3.3 The appeal

You can appeal a decision once, from its statement, within [[FOUNDER: appeal-window — how long after a decision an appeal can be made]]. Say why you consider the decision wrong. A person reviews your appeal within 7 days and sends you the outcome with its reasons (section 3.11). Whatever the outcome, you can also take the matter to court. [[COUNSEL: redress — Article 20 does not bind a micro or small platform: must this appeal still follow its rules, such as six months to appeal and a decision not taken solely by automated means, and must the statement name out-of-court dispute settlement bodies? Counsel brief B4(2).]]

3.4 Item removed

“DressYou has removed your post. Nobody can see it any more, in any country. It stays removed unless your appeal succeeds.”

3.5 Item hidden during review

“DressYou has hidden your post while a person reviews a report about it. It is hidden from others until the review ends, within 24 hours.”

If the review finds no breach, the post becomes visible again and DressYou says so; otherwise the decision in section 3.4 follows.

3.6 Post held before publication

“Your post is waiting for a person to review it before it appears. Every post showing swimwear or underwear waits for this review, as does any post that automatic screening holds. The review takes up to 24 hours.”

3.7 Held post not published

“A person has reviewed your post, and DressYou will not publish it.”

3.8 Account suspended

“DressYou has suspended your account.” The statement says what the suspension covers and when it ends. [[FOUNDER: suspension-effect — What does a suspension stop, such as posting, commenting, earning rewards or signing in; what stays available, such as export and deletion; and how long can it last?]]

3.9 Account closed

“DressYou has closed your account.” The statement says what happens to the account's data. [[FOUNDER: closure-effect — What happens to a closed account's data, and can the person export it first?]]

3.10 Rewards withheld

“DressYou has withheld the renders earned from these try-ons, because they did not come from genuine engagement.” The statement lists the try-ons concerned and the number of renders withheld. [[COUNSEL: rewards-as-payments — Is withholding earned renders a restriction of monetary payments under Article 17(1)(b), although renders have no cash value?]]

3.11 Appeal decided

Decision confirmed: “A person has reviewed your appeal and confirmed the decision, for the reasons below.”

Decision reversed: “A person has reviewed your appeal and reversed the decision.” The statement says what has been restored.

Both end: “You can still take the matter to court.”

3.12 Decision on a notice, to the person who sent it

Action taken: “DressYou has reviewed your report and acted on it.” The statement names the measure.

No action: “DressYou has reviewed your report and found that the item breaks neither the law nor the terms of use. It stays online.”

Both end: “You can take the matter to court.” [[COUNSEL: notifier-redress — Must the person who sent a notice also be offered the appeal, as Article 20 would allow?]]

3.13 Grounds

ReasonGroundExplanation given
Not the poster's own photographTerms of use, section 8.1A post must be a real photograph of the poster wearing clothes they own.
Generated imageTerms of use, section 8.1A post may not be a generated image, including a twin or a try-on.
Garments aloneTerms of use, section 8.1A post must show the poster wearing the clothes; a photograph of garments alone is not allowed.
Someone pictured without their agreementTerms of use, sections 8.1 and 8.4Anyone else pictured must have agreed to appear.
Text that disparages someone's bodyTerms of use, section 8.4Captions, hashtags and comments may not disparage anyone's body.
Harassment or threatsTerms of use, section 8.4Harassment and threats are not allowed.
Sexual contentTerms of use, section 8.4Sexual content is not allowed.
Impersonation or fake accountTerms of use, sections 8.4 and 15An account may not impersonate anyone, and fake accounts are not allowed.
Spam, undisclosed advertising or manufactured engagementTerms of use, sections 8.4 and 9Spam, undisclosed advertising and engagement manufactured to earn rewards are not allowed.
Infringement of another person's rightsTerms of use, section 8.4Content may not infringe another person's rights, including their copyright and their image.
Illegal contentThe law named in the statementThe statement explains why the content is illegal under that law.
